My partner and I visited 3Sixty for my birthday, expecting a top-notch dining experience. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the most disappointing restaurant visits we have ever had.

Our reservation was at 7:00 PM. When we arrived, no one greeted us despite staff repeatedly walking past the entrance. There was no acknowledgment or indication that someone would be with us shortly. After several minutes, we were finally seated and placed our order at 7:15 PM.

The first item to arrive was bread and butter, which took approximately 25 minutes. We then waited another 45 minutes for our three starters, only to discover that one of them had been forgotten. When I asked about the missing dish, our server looked surprised, rushed to the kitchen, and never returned to explain the situation. I had to repeatedly try to get her attention and finally managed to do so about 10 minutes later. She simply said the starter was on its way. There was no explanation, no apology, and no attempt to recover the situation.

We had informed the staff from the beginning that we intended to share the starters, yet no extra plates were provided. In my experience, this is basic etiquette in any restaurant that positions itself as upscale.

While we were still eating our starters, another staff member came to clear our plates and stood beside the table waiting for us to finish. It was uncomfortable and unprofessional.

We each had a glass of wine, and once the glasses were empty, nobody asked whether we would like another drink. This is a basic part of attentive service, especially in a restaurant of this caliber.

After the starters, we waited another 45 minutes or more for our main courses, which finally arrived around 9:00 PM. By then, the mood was completely ruined. My partner, who had planned this evening as a birthday celebration for me, was ready to leave. I chose to stay in the hope that the restaurant might acknowledge the poor service and excessive delays in some way, perhaps with a complimentary dessert. Nothing of the sort happened.

What makes this even more surprising is that the restaurant was far from full. It was a Tuesday evening, yet the service was painfully slow throughout the entire visit.

The food itself was equally disappointing. I ordered the fish, and the sauce tasted like a poor imitation of mashed canned ratatouille. My partner ordered the meat, which was completely lacking in flavor. Nobody asked how he would like it cooked, and nobody checked whether we were satisfied with our meals.

The staff seemed far more interested in their phones and chatting with each other than paying attention to guests. The server responsible for our table appeared more focused on socializing with another staff member than monitoring her customers. The bartender was also frequently scrolling through his phone rather than engaging with guests.

I have dined all over the world, from budget restaurants to Michelin-starred establishments, and this was genuinely one of the worst experiences I have ever had in terms of both service and food quality.

The impression I got is that the restaurant relies heavily on its rooftop location and impressive views. However, views alone cannot compensate for poor service, long waiting times, and mediocre food. Unless significant improvements are made to the menu, food quality, and staff training, I struggle to see how the restaurant can maintain its reputation.

My advice: if you are desperate for the rooftop view, stop by for a drink, assuming the bartender can put down his phone long enough to serve you. Then head to the burger restaurant next door. You’ll likely leave much happier, better fed, and with a far more enjoyable experience.

I work as a Foodora rider and would like to draw attention to a very unpleasant incident that occurred at McDonald’s Barkarby in Järfälla on 06/06 between approximately 20:40 and 21:15.

I waited 10 minutes for a customer order and asked the shift manager Navraj how long it would take. I was then told that if I did not want to wait any longer, I could cancel the order and leave the restaurant.

After this, I took out my phone at the checkout to check how long I had waited and to write down the name of the responsible manager so that I could remember it later when I wanted to file a complaint about the service.

Then Navraj suddenly took my phone right out of my hand and put it in his pocket. When I asked to get my phone back, he initially refused to give it back. I explained that it was my private phone and that otherwise I would have to contact the police or security guard, but was told that I could do whatever I wanted. Since my phone was in his pocket, I couldn't contact anyone either.

It wasn't until about 10 minutes later, and after several people in the restaurant had told him to return the phone, that I got it back.

I find this behavior completely unacceptable. No matter the situation, no one has the right to take someone else's private phone and refuse to return it. I hope the restaurant manager or management in charge sees this review, reviews the surveillance cameras from the time, and investigates the incident. I also hope that appropriate action is taken so that neither customers nor delivery drivers have to experience anything like this in the future.
